correlations.description: The available evidence suggests f0, f1, f2, f3 and f4 belong to the same Phase 2D incident anomaly/Shooting/Shooting037_x264.mp4:i0 in anomaly/Shooting/Shooting037_x264.mp4.
The surveillance-event model produced compatible Shooting hypotheses persistently across adjacent windows from 0.0s to 10.134s.
Shooting hypotheses co-occurred with car detections and driving car hypotheses in the same windows; the evidence is consistent with source agreement only and does not confirm an event.

inferences.text: The available evidence suggests persistent co-occurrence of vehicle-related detections and Shooting model hypotheses throughout 0.0s to 10.134s, but is insufficient to establish that a shooting definitely occurred or to identify any persons involved.

limitations: No access to CCTV footage; reasoning is limited to supplied model outputs.
Model labels such as Shooting and driving car are hypotheses and must not be treated as confirmed crimes or actions.
No person detections or identity information were supplied, so involvement of any person cannot be assessed.
Small temporal gaps between cited windows were not covered by evidence.

observation.text: The evidence indicates the surveillance-event model produced a Shooting hypothesis in each window from 0.0s to 10.134s, while the object model detected cars (counts 2-4) and the generic-action model produced a driving car hypothesis in the same windows.
